subject: maths
stem: In which quadrant does the point (−3, 5) lie?
rationale: A negative x and a positive y put the point left of the y-axis and above the x-axis: the second quadrant. Fourth is the sign swap (x positive, y negative).

subject: maths
stem: What is the distance between the points (1, 2) and (4, 6)?
rationale: The differences are 3 and 4, so the distance is √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5. Adding the differences (7) is the error the numeric format leaves uncued.

subject: maths
stem: What is the midpoint of the line segment joining (2, −4) and (8, 6)?
rationale: Average each coordinate: ((2 + 8)/2, (−4 + 6)/2) = (5, 1). (10, 2) forgets to halve; (6, 10) and (3, 5) subtract instead of adding.

subject: maths
stem: What is the zero of the polynomial p(x) = 3x − 12?
rationale: The zero is the x that makes p(x) = 0: 3x − 12 = 0 gives x = 4. −4 is the sign slip; 3 and 12 are the coefficients read off as answers.

subject: maths
stem: If p(x) = 5 − 2x, what is the value of p(−3)?
rationale: p(−3) = 5 − 2 × (−3) = 5 + 6 = 11. Dropping the sign of −3 gives −1, the characteristic error.

subject: maths
stem: Which of these numbers is irrational?
rationale: √12 = 2√3, and √3 is irrational. √16 = 4, 0.75 = 3/4 and 22/7 are all ratios of integers; 22/7 is only an approximation to π, not π itself.

subject: maths
stem: Which of these fractions has a terminating decimal expansion?
rationale: A fraction in lowest terms terminates when its denominator has no prime factor but 2 and 5. 20 = 2² × 5, so 7/20 = 0.35. 3, 7 and 6 each bring a 3 or a 7.

subject: maths
stem: Which expression is equal to (x + 5)²?
rationale: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b², so (x + 5)² = x² + 10x + 25. x² + 25 misses the middle term, the commonest error with this identity.

subject: maths
stem: An arc of a circle subtends an angle of 80° at the centre. What angle does it subtend at a point on the remaining part of the circle?
rationale: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at any point on the remaining part of the circle, so 80° ÷ 2 = 40°. 160° doubles the wrong way; 100° confuses it with a supplement.

subject: maths
stem: A circle has a radius of 10 cm. A chord is 6 cm from the centre. How long is the chord, in centimetres?
rationale: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, so half the chord is √(10² − 6²) = 8 cm and the chord is 16 cm. Stopping at 8 is the error being tested.

subject: maths
stem: Using a suitable identity, find the value of 103 × 97.
rationale: 103 × 97 = (100 + 3)(100 − 3) = 100² − 3² = 10000 − 9 = 9991. 10009 adds the 9; 9919 and 9909 come from slips in long multiplication.

subject: maths
stem: A plant is 12 cm tall and grows 1.5 cm every week, so its height after w weeks is 12 + 1.5w. After how many weeks will it be 30 cm tall?
rationale: 12 + 1.5w = 30 gives 1.5w = 18, so w = 12. Dividing 30 by 1.5 (20) forgets the starting height, which is what the item checks.

subject: maths
stem: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral with ∠A = (2x + 10)° and ∠C = (3x − 5)°. What is the measure of ∠A?
rationale: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°: 5x + 5 = 180, so x = 35 and ∠A = 80°. 100° is ∠C; setting the angles equal gives x = 15 and 40°, which is not offered.

subject: maths
stem: Which of these is a factor of x² − 5x − 14?
rationale: Split −5x into −7x + 2x: the numbers multiply to −14 and add to −5, so x² − 5x − 14 = (x − 7)(x + 2). x + 7 and x − 2 have the signs reversed.

subject: maths
stem: Point P divides the line segment from A(2, 1) to B(8, 7) in the ratio 1 : 2. What are the coordinates of P?
rationale: P is one third of the way from A to B: (2 + 6/3, 1 + 6/3) = (4, 3). (6, 5) is the 2 : 1 point, the ratio read backwards; (5, 4) is the midpoint.

subject: science
stem: A runner goes 4 m east and then 3 m west along a straight track. What is the runner's displacement?
rationale: Displacement is the change in position: 4 m east less 3 m west leaves 1 m east. 7 m is the distance travelled, which is the distinction the item tests.

subject: science
stem: A cyclist rides 12 km in the first hour and 8 km in the second hour. What is the average speed for the whole ride, in km/h?
rationale: Average speed is total distance over total time: 20 km in 2 h is 10 km/h. Here the times are equal, so the plain average of the two speeds also works.

subject: science
stem: A car's velocity increases steadily from 10 m/s to 25 m/s in 5 seconds. What is its average acceleration?
rationale: Acceleration is the change in velocity over time: (25 − 10) ÷ 5 = 3 m/s². 2 m/s² divides the starting speed by the time; 5 m/s² (25 ÷ 5) is not offered.

subject: science
stem: What is the momentum of a 2 kg ball moving at 3 m/s, in kg m/s?
rationale: Momentum is mass × velocity: 2 kg × 3 m/s = 6 kg m/s. Adding the two (5) is the error a candidate who half-remembers the definition makes.

subject: science
stem: What net force is needed to give a 5 kg box an acceleration of 2 m/s²?
rationale: F = ma = 5 kg × 2 m/s² = 10 N. 2.5 N divides instead of multiplying; 7 N and 3 N add and subtract the numbers.

subject: science
stem: Which part of a cell releases energy from food and is often called the powerhouse of the cell?
rationale: Mitochondria carry out cellular respiration, releasing energy from food. The nucleus controls the cell, the vacuole stores, and the membrane controls what enters and leaves.

subject: science
stem: Which of these is found in plant cells but not in animal cells?
rationale: Plant cells have a rigid cell wall outside the membrane; animal cells do not. Both kinds have a membrane, a nucleus and mitochondria.

subject: science
stem: Which plant tissue carries water and minerals from the roots to the leaves?
rationale: Xylem conducts water and minerals upward from the roots. Phloem carries food made in the leaves, the usual confusion; epidermis and cork protect.

subject: science
stem: Which method is best for separating sand from a mixture of sand and water?
rationale: Sand does not dissolve, so filter paper holds it back while water passes through. Evaporation and distillation recover a dissolved solid or the liquid; chromatography separates dyes.

subject: science
stem: Raisins left in a bowl of water swell up after a few hours. This is mainly because

options.B: sugar moves into them from the water
options.C: their skin soaks up air bubbles
options.D: warmth in the water expands them

rationale: The raisin's cells hold a strong sugar solution, so water moves in across the membrane by osmosis. Sugar moves out, if anything, not in.

subject: science
stem: On a velocity–time graph, the line for a car is horizontal and above the time axis. The car is
rationale: A horizontal line means the velocity does not change, and above the axis means it is not zero. Standing still is what a horizontal line means on a position–time graph.

subject: science
stem: Which method separates the different coloured dyes that make up black ink?
rationale: The dyes are dissolved together, and chromatography separates them because each travels a different distance with the solvent. Filtering and decanting cannot split a solution.

subject: science
stem: A ball starts from rest and rolls down a slope with a uniform acceleration of 2 m/s². How far does it travel in 4 seconds, in metres?
rationale: From rest, s = ½at² = ½ × 2 × 4² = 16 m. Forgetting the half gives 32; using v = at (8) answers a different question.

subject: science
stem: Two skaters stand at rest on ice. The 50 kg skater pushes the 25 kg skater, who moves off at 2 m/s. How fast does the 50 kg skater move back?
rationale: Total momentum stays zero, so 50 × v = 25 × 2 and v = 1 m/s, in the opposite direction. 4 m/s inverts the mass ratio.

subject: science
stem: A car moving at 20 m/s brakes with a uniform deceleration of 5 m/s² until it stops. How far does it travel while braking?
rationale: v² = u² − 2as gives 0 = 400 − 10s, so s = 40 m. Equivalently, it takes 4 s at an average 10 m/s. 80 m uses the full 20 m/s for all 4 s.
